p.challenge: Count Kabir's joint family. How many people live together, Kabir included?

p.title: Helping Nanu
p.challenge: Help Asha care for Nanu. Choose at each step and play to the end.

nodes.text: Nanu wants to read the newspaper
nodes.info: As people grow old, they may walk slowly, see less clearly or forget things.

nodes.text: Can he find his glasses?
Fetch his glasses, or read the news aloud to him
nodes.info: His glasses are in the next room.

nodes.text: He reads. Sit with him and listen
nodes.info: Elders have lots of love and lots of stories.

nodes.text: Going for a walk together?
Walk slowly beside him
nodes.info: Match his speed so he does not have to hurry.

nodes.text: Talk politely and listen to him
nodes.info: Spending time and talking with elders makes them happy.

p.itemName: a balloon (₹10) and a plate of jalebi (₹30)
p.challenge: At the mela, Tara buys a balloon (₹10) and jalebi (₹30). She pays ₹50. Give her the right change.

p.title: Safe at the mela
p.challenge: Play both paths. What should you do if you get lost at the mela?

nodes.text: At the mela with your grown-up
nodes.info: Fix a meeting place, like the big gate, in case you get separated.

nodes.text: Are you lost?
Stay close and hold their hand
nodes.info: Always stay close to your grown-up in a crowd.

nodes.text: Stay calm. Stay where you are
nodes.info: Do not wander around looking.

nodes.text: A stranger offers sweets or toys?
Go to a help desk or a police officer
nodes.info: They can help you find your family.

nodes.text: Say no. Never go with a stranger
Enjoy the mela together!
Tell your name, parent's name and phone number
nodes.info: Learn them by heart.

p.title: Journey of water in a plant
p.challenge: Put the water's journey in order: from the soil up to the leaves.

nodes.text: Water in the soil
nodes.info: Rainwater soaks into the soil.

nodes.text: Roots take in the water
nodes.info: Roots grow under the soil. They also hold the plant firmly.

nodes.text: The stem carries water up
nodes.info: The stem holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.

nodes.text: Water reaches the leaves
nodes.info: Leaves are joined to the stem by a small stalk.

nodes.text: Leaves make food with sunlight, air and water
nodes.info: This food helps the whole plant grow.

p.title: From flower to seed
p.challenge: Rohit saw bees on the mustard flowers. Put the steps in order, from flower to new plant.
panels: Mustard plants grow yellow flowers.
Bees buzz around the flowers.
The flowers turn into thin pods (fruits).
Seeds grow inside the pods.
A seed grows into a new mustard plant.

p.title: How do seeds travel?
p.challenge: Try every path: how do cotton seeds, coconuts and fruit seeds reach new places?

nodes.text: A seed needs to travel to a new place
Is it light and fluffy?
It flies with the wind
nodes.info: Cotton and aak (madar) seeds fly with the wind.

nodes.text: Can it float?
It floats on water
nodes.info: Coconuts float on water to new places.

nodes.text: Birds eat the fruit and drop the seed
nodes.info: Birds drop seeds of fruits they eat.

p.challenge: A tiger never eats grass. Build a chain from a plant to the tiger to show it still needs plants!

p.title: How bees and birds help plants
p.challenge: Put the 6 steps in order: from a bee on a flower to a new plant.

nodes.text: A bee visits a flower for nectar
Yellow pollen sticks to the bee
nodes.info: Pollen is a yellow powder in flowers.

nodes.text: The bee carries pollen to another flower
nodes.info: This helps flowers make fruits and seeds.

nodes.text: The flower grows into a fruit with seeds
A bird eats the fruit
The seed is dropped far away and grows
nodes.info: New plants can grow in new places.

places.name: Chipko movement

places.name: Bishnoi people

p.challenge: Tap 4 places and the river to learn about sources of water.

places.name: Gangotri glacier
places.info: Snow and ice on high mountains melt and flow into rivers. The Ganga starts here.

places.name: Rani ki Vav
places.info: A stepwell in Gujarat, built long ago to store water.

places.name: Chand Baori
places.info: A stepwell in Rajasthan, built long ago to store water.

places.name: Chennai
places.info: Chennai is by the sea, but sea water is too salty to drink.

lines.name: Ganga
lines.info: Melted snow from the Gangotri glacier and rainwater fill the river Ganga.

p.title: Is it safe to drink?
p.challenge: Raju wants a glass of water. Play both paths: how do we make water safe to drink?

nodes.text: You want a glass of drinking water
Is the water clean and safe?
nodes.info: Drinking water must be clean.

nodes.text: Boil it and let it cool, or filter it
nodes.info: Boiling or filtering water makes it safe to drink.

nodes.text: Drink it!
nodes.info: Clean water keeps us healthy.

p.title: How is it cooked?
p.challenge: Idli batter sits over boiling water and never touches it. Answer the questions to find how idlis are cooked.

nodes.text: How is this food cooked?
nodes.info: Cooking is always done by or with an adult!

nodes.text: Is it eaten raw?
Eaten raw: fruits, salad
nodes.info: Fruits, cucumbers and carrots in a salad are eaten raw.

nodes.text: Cooked in hot oil?
Frying: puris, pakoras, samosas
nodes.info: Frying: cooking in hot oil.

nodes.text: Cooked in hot bubbling water?
Boiling: rice, dal, eggs
nodes.info: Boiling: cooking in hot bubbling water.

nodes.text: Cooked with steam from boiling water?
Steaming: idlis, dhoklas, modaks
nodes.info: Steaming: cooking with steam from boiling water. Idlis never touch the water!

nodes.text: Cooked over a flame?
Roasting: bhutta
nodes.info: Roasting cooks food over a flame.

nodes.text: Baking in an oven: bread, cake
nodes.info: Baking cooks food in an oven.

nodes.text: Meera's lunch: rice
nodes.info: Rice is an energy-giving food.

nodes.text: Is there a body-building food?
nodes.info: Dal, milk, paneer, eggs and fish help us grow strong.

nodes.text: Add dal or curd
Is there a fruit or vegetable?
nodes.info: Fruits and vegetables are protective foods.

nodes.text: Add a vegetable or a fruit
A balanced meal! Drink clean water too

nodes.text: Shape it on the spinning wheel (chaak)

p.title: What kind of waste?
p.challenge: Sort the waste! Is a banana peel wet or dry? A plastic wrapper? An old battery? Play each path.

nodes.text: What kind of waste is it?
Does it come from plants or food?
Wet waste: it rots and mixes with soil
nodes.info: Peels, leftover food, tea leaves, fallen leaves.

nodes.text: Is it a battery, medicine or broken bulb?
Harmful waste: an adult must hand it over
nodes.info: Never play with it.

nodes.text: Dry waste: paper, plastic, glass, metal, cloth
nodes.info: Most dry waste does not rot quickly. Plastic does not rot at all.

p.title: Making compost
p.challenge: Put the compost steps in order. See how waste goes back to plants!
panels: Collect wet waste: peels and leftover food
Put it in a pit or a pot
Cover it with soil or dry leaves
Wait some weeks. Earthworms and tiny living things break it down
It becomes compost, a rich manure
Compost helps plants grow, and plants give us food

nodes.text: Old newspapers pile up at home
The kabadiwala buys them
nodes.info: The kabadiwala buys old newspapers, bottles and metal.

nodes.text: They are sent for recycling
Old paper is made into new paper
nodes.info: Recycle means turning old things into new things.

nodes.text: We use the new paper
